source.verbatim_statement: The benefit of using an exact interval is obvious: one does not risk that the actual coverage falls below \(1-\alpha\).

attestation.note: Transcribed from the published author's manuscript, arXiv:1303.1288, Section 1; Section 2.1 identifies the exact interval as the two-sided Clopper--Pearson inversion.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The proof uses exact marginal Clopper--Pearson coverage, so the cited leaf must be recorded in the proposition's forward dependency metadata.

proposed.justification: This corollary records the direct Bonferroni consequence of simultaneous multinomial cell-law coverage and definitional set inversion.
proposed.gap: Relative to Chernozhukov, Hong, and Tamer and the constrained inversion in Dobronyi, Gu, Kim, and Russell, this is only a model-specific exact finite-sample inversion corollary, not an independent inference theorem.
proposed.consumer: The PSID robustness analysis can attach conservative simultaneous coverage to every slope and APE compatible with the population law.
